### Q1. JEE Advanced 2024 (Paper 2)

*Type:* `numerical` | *Level:* `2`

A spherical soap bubble inside an air chamber at pressure $P_0=10^5 \mathrm{~Pa}$ has a certain radius so that the excess pressure inside the bubble is $\Delta P=144 \mathrm{~Pa}$. Now, the chamber pressure is reduced to $8 P_0 / 27$ so that the bubble radius and its excess pressure change. In this process, all the temperatures remain unchanged. Assume air to be an ideal gas and the excess pressure $\Delta P$ in both the cases to be much smaller than the chamber pressure. The new excess pressure $\Delta P$ in $\mathrm{Pa}$ is ________ .

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Value:** **96**

**Detailed Solution:**

Case-1
<img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_advanced/xSQx_PDIl80GdgaqClFg7-K6KutQR5OqkvpnIN1hAh0.original.fullsize.png">
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}_0=\Delta \mathrm{P}=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}} \\ & \mathrm{P}=\left(\mathrm{P}_0+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)\end{aligned}$
Case-2
<img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_advanced/wo2OsYqeua56C6mDSoRN3Ulr-kdD7R1_KrDMH2MzxMc.original.fullsize.png">
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}_1-\frac{8 \mathrm{P}_0}{27}=\Delta \mathrm{P}_1=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}_1} \\ & \mathrm{P}_1=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}_1}+\frac{8 \mathrm{P}_0}{27}\end{aligned}$
Constant temperature process
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{PV}=\mathrm{P}_1 \mathrm{~V}_1 \\ & \left(\mathrm{P}_0+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}}\right) \frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3=\left(\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}_1}+\frac{8 \mathrm{P}_0}{27}\right) \frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}_1^3 ;\left(\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}}\right),\left(\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}_1}\right) \rightarrow \text { (Neglected) } \\ & \mathrm{R}=\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{R}_1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_1=\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{R} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{P}_1=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}_1}=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{3 \mathrm{R}} \times 2=\frac{2}{3} \times(144)=96 \mathrm{~Pa}\end{aligned}$

</details>

### Q3. JEE Advanced 2020 (Paper 1)

*Type:* `numerical` | *Level:* `3`

<p>When water is filled carefully in a glass, one can fill it to a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> above the rim of the glass due to the surface tension of water. To calculate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> just before water starts flowing, model the shape of the water above the rim as a disc of thickness <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> having semicircular edges, as shown schematically in the figure. When the pressure of water at the bottom of this disc exceeds what can be withstood due to the surface tension, the water surface breaks near the rim and water starts flowing from there. If the density of water, its surface tension and the acceleration due to gravity are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>07</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mm</mi></math>) is ________.</p><p><img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_advanced/9bc3707a-5c38-41b6-a184-1946494c169e-image.png"/></p>

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Value:** **3.74**

**Detailed Solution:**

<img src=" data:image/png;base64,">
Pressure at the bottom of disc \(=\) pressure due to surface tension
\(\begin{aligned}
&\rho g h=T\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2}\right) \\
&\mathrm{R}_1 \gg>\mathrm{R}_2 \\
&\text { So } \frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1} \ll<\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2} \text { and } \mathrm{R}_2=\mathrm{h} / 2 \\
&\therefore \rho \mathrm{gh}=\mathrm{T}\left[\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2}\right]=\mathrm{T}\left[0+\frac{1}{\mathrm{~h} / 2}\right] \\
&\mathrm{h}^2=\frac{2 \mathrm{~T}}{\rho \mathrm{g}} \\
&\mathrm{h}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{~T}}{\rho \mathrm{g}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \times 0.07}{10^3 \times 10}}=\sqrt{\frac{14 \times 100}{10^4 \times 100}} \\
&\mathrm{~h}=\sqrt{14} \mathrm{~mm}=3.741
\end{aligned}\)

</details>

*Type:* `multipleCorrect` | *Level:* `2`

<p>A cylindrical capillary tube of <math><mn>0.2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> radius is made by joining two capillaries <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> of different materials having water contact angles of <math><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup></math> and <math><msup><mrow><mn>60</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></math> respectively. (Surface tension of water <math><mo>=</mo><mn>0.075</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></mrow></math> density of water <math><mo>=</mo><mn>1000</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow></mrow></math> take <math><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></math>
<img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_advanced/qmseeagfrbqbbpolvlocklqjkhzvpshgqyojiasyhcbocthism.png"/></p>

**Options:**

- **(A)** For case II, if the capillary joint is  <math><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>  above the water surface, the height of water column raised in the tube will be  <math><mn>3.75</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo></math>  (Neglect the weight of the water in the meniscus)
- **(B)** For case I, if the joint is kept at  <math><mn>8</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>  above the water surface, the height of water column in the tube will be  <math><mn>7.5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo></math>  (Neglect the weight of the water in the meniscus)
- **(C)** The correction in the height of water column raised in the tube, due to weight of water contained in the meniscus, will be different for both cases.
- **(D)** For case I, if the capillary joint is  <math><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>  above the water surface, the height of water column raised in the tube will be more than  <math><mn>8.75</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo></math>  (Neglect the weight of the water in the meniscus)

<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(C) The correction in the height of water column raised in the tube, due to weight of water contained in the meniscus, will be different for both cases.**

**Detailed Solution:**

Heights if only single material tubes are used of sufficient length,

For table  <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>0.075</mn><mo>×</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>K</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1000</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo>×</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>7.5</mn><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> 

For table  <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⇒</mo><msub><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><msup><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>′</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>0.075</mn><mo>×</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1000</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo>×</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3.75</mn><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>

Also the length of tube available is  <math><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> .

### Q5. JEE Advanced 2018 (Paper 1)

*Type:* `multipleCorrect` | *Level:* `2`

A uniform capillary tube of inner radius <math><mi>r</mi></math> is dipped vertically into a beaker filled with water. The water rises to a height <math><mi>h</mi></math> in the capillary tube above the water surface in the beaker. The surface tension of water is <math><mi>&#963;</mi></math> . The angle of contact between water and the wall of the capillary tube is <math><mi>&#952;</mi></math> . Ignore the mass of water in the meniscus. Which of the following statements is (are) true?

**Options:**

- **(A)** For a given material of the capillary tube, <math><mi>h</mi></math> decreases with increase in <math><mi>r</mi></math>
- **(B)** For a given material of the capillary tube,  <math><mi>h</mi></math>  is independent of  <math><mi>σ</mi></math>
- **(C)** If this experiment is performed in a lift going up with a constant acceleration, then <math><mi>h</mi></math> decreases
- **(D)** <math><mi>h</mi></math>  is proportional to contact angle  <math><mi>θ</mi></math>

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(C) If this experiment is performed in a lift going up with a constant acceleration, then <math><mi>h</mi></math> decreases**

**Detailed Solution:**

<math><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>h</mi></math> <math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>
<math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>ρ</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow></mfrac></math> <math><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cos</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></math> [r→radius of capillary; <math><mi>θ</mi><mo>→</mo></math> contact angle]

### Q8. JEE Advanced 2010 (Paper 2)

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Level:* `1`

<strong>Paragraph:</strong>
When liquid medicine of density $\rho$ is to be put in the eye, it is done with the help of a dropper. As the bulb on the top of the dropper is pressed, a drop forms at the opening of the dropper. We wish to estimate the size of the drop.
We first assume that the drop formed at the opening is spherical because that requires a minimum increase in its surface energy. To determine the size, we calculate the net vertical force due to the surface tension $T$ when the radius of the drop is $R$. When this force becomes smaller than the weight of the drop, the drop gets detached from the dropper.<strong>Question:</strong>
After the drop detaches, its surface energy is

**Options:**

- **(A)** $1.4 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~J}$
- **(B)** $2.7 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~J}$
- **(C)** $5.4 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~J}$
- **(D)** $8.1 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~J}$

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(B) $2.7 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~J}$**

**Detailed Solution:**

Surface energy,
$$
\begin{aligned}
E & =\left(4 \pi R^2\right) T \\
& =(4 \pi)\left(1.4 \times 10^{-3}\right)^2(0.11) \\
& =2.7 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~J}
\end{aligned}
$$
$\therefore$ The correct option is (b).

</details>

---

### Q9. JEE Advanced 2010 (Paper 2)

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Level:* `1`

<strong>Paragraph:</strong>
When liquid medicine of density $\rho$ is to be put in the eye, it is done with the help of a dropper. As the bulb on the top of the dropper is pressed, a drop forms at the opening of the dropper. We wish to estimate the size of the drop.
We first assume that the drop formed at the opening is spherical because that requires a minimum increase in its surface energy. To determine the size, we calculate the net vertical force due to the surface tension $T$ when the radius of the drop is $R$. When this force becomes smaller than the weight of the drop, the drop gets detached from the dropper.<strong>Question:</strong>
If $r=5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}, \rho=10^3 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$, $g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}, T=0.11 \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$, the radius of the drop when it detaches from the dropper is approximately

**Options:**

- **(A)** $1.4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$
- **(B)** $3.3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$
- **(C)** $2.0 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$
- **(D)** $4.1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(A) $1.4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$**

**Detailed Solution:**

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{2 \pi r^2 T}{R}=m g=\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 \cdot \rho \cdot g \\
& \begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad R^4 & =\frac{3 r^2 T}{2 \rho g}=\frac{3 \times\left(5 \times 10^{-4}\right)^2(0.11)}{2 \times 10^3 \times 10} \\
& =4.125 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~m}^4
\end{aligned} \\
& \therefore R=1.425 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m} \approx 1.4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m} \\
& \therefore \text { The correct option is (a). }
\end{aligned}
$$

</details>

---

### Q10. JEE Advanced 2010 (Paper 2)

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Level:* `2`

<strong>Paragraph:</strong>
When liquid medicine of density $\rho$ is to be put in the eye, it is done with the help of a dropper. As the bulb on the top of the dropper is pressed, a drop forms at the opening of the dropper. We wish to estimate the size of the drop.
We first assume that the drop formed at the opening is spherical because that requires a minimum increase in its surface energy. To determine the size, we calculate the net vertical force due to the surface tension $T$ when the radius of the drop is $R$. When this force becomes smaller than the weight of the drop, the drop gets detached from the dropper.<strong>Question:</strong>
If the radius of the opening of the dropper is $r$, the vertical force due to the surface tension on the drop of radius $R$ (assuming $r< < R$ ) is

**Options:**

- **(A)** $2 \pi r T$
- **(B)** $2 \pi R T$
- **(C)** $\frac{2 \pi r^2 T}{R}$
- **(D)** $\frac{2 \pi R^2 T}{r}$

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(C) $\frac{2 \pi r^2 T}{R}$**

**Detailed Solution:**

Vertical force due to surface tension,
<img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_advanced/o4deu4ddbC-5yG25YqfzhyYmEFYug3P_Lf7lKpjW0tY.original.fullsize.png">

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_v & =F \sin \theta=(T \cdot 2 \pi r)(r / R) \\
& =\frac{2 \pi r^2 T}{R}
\end{aligned}
$$
$\therefore$ The correct option is (c).

</details>

### Q11. JEE Advanced 2008 (Paper 2)

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Level:* `2`

A glass tube of uniform internal radius $(r)$ has a valve separating the two identical ends. Initially, the valve is in a tightly closed position. End 1 has a hemispherical soap bubble of radius $r$. End 2 has sub-hemispherical soap bubble as shown in figure. Just after opening the valve,
<img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_advanced/aTOnsM_ko_rZ4DTOZ1tXO4djJRRDKbR9XCHC2FJmEWk.original.fullsize.png">

**Options:**

- **(A)** air from end 1 flows towards end 2. No change in the volume of the soap bubbles
- **(B)** air from end 1 flows towards end 2. Volume of the soap bubble at end 1 decreases
- **(C)** no change occurs
- **(D)** air from end 2 flows towards end 1. Volume of the soap bubble at end 1 increases

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(B) air from end 1 flows towards end 2. Volume of the soap bubble at end 1 decreases**

**Detailed Solution:**

$\Delta p_1=\frac{4 T}{r_1}$ and $\Delta p_2=\frac{4 T}{r_2}$
$$
\begin{array}{cc} 
& r_1 < r_2 \\
\therefore & \Delta p_1>\Delta p_2
\end{array}
$$
Air will flow from 1 to 2 and volume of bubble at end- 1 will decrease.
Therefore, correct option is (b).

</details>

### Q12. JEE Advanced 2007 (Paper 2)

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Level:* `3`

Water is filled up to a height $h$ in a beaker of radius $R$ as shown in the figure. The density of water is $\rho$, the surface tension of water is $T$ and the atmospheric pressure is $p_0$. Consider a vertical section $A B C D$ of the water column through a diameter of the beaker. The force on water on one side of this section by water on the other side of this section has magnitude.
<img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_advanced/U9L6A5gFosJxDI2DolDICI2XIMxNUvXy__El6qT0wVI.original.fullsize.png">

**Options:**

- **(A)** $\left|2 p_0 R h+\pi R^2 \rho g h-2 R T\right|$
- **(B)** $\left|2 p_0 R h+R \rho g h^2-2 R T\right|$
- **(C)** $\left|p_0 \pi R^2+R \rho g h^2-2 R T\right|$
- **(D)** $\left|p_0 \pi R^2+R \rho g h^2+2 R T\right|$

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(B) $\left|2 p_0 R h+R \rho g h^2-2 R T\right|$**

**Detailed Solution:**

Force from right hand side liquid on left hand side liquid.
(i) Due to surface tension force $=2 R T$ (towards right)
(ii) Due to liquid pressure force
$$
\begin{aligned}
& =\int_{x=0}^{x=h}\left(p_0+\rho g h\right)(2 R \cdot x) d x \\
& =\left(2 p_0 R h+R \rho g h^2\right) \text { (towards left) }
\end{aligned}
$$
$\therefore$ Net force is $\left|2 p_0 R h+R \rho g h^2-2 R T\right|$ Correct option is (b).

</details>

---
